item.title: Portugal's last circus elephant adapts to life in new sanctuary, gaining 100kg
item.description: 'She can be in any habitat, she literally owns everything, she makes her own choices,' says the manager of the Pangea Sanctuary.

item.title: French pupils step up protests as government concessions fall flat
item.description: Unions walked out of talks with the prime minister’s office over the presence of the far right, while firework mortars have been set off inside schools as tensions rise.

item.title: Ukraine and Russia reportedly show 'a little bit of flexibility' on territory as Abu Dhabi talks begin
item.description: The renewed US-mediated negotiations come amid deep divisions over territorial concessions and post-war security guarantees, with European leaders pressing for a role in discussions that could reshape the continent's security.

item.title: EPSO: Italian applicant boom puts EU hiring balance to the test
item.description: The EPSO generalist exam started on November 9, but almost half of the applicants come from one single country, Italy. This clashes with the Commission's own hiring rules, which favour 'underrepresented countries' to address geographical staff imbalances.

item.title: Senegal: Footage reveals wreckage of deadly migrant boat in which 39 people died
item.description: At least 39 people have died after a migrant boat sank off Senegal's Atlantic coast. Footage shows the shattered vessel washed ashore as rescuers continue searching for victims.

item.title: Trump says Nvidia CEO Huang knew nothing about alleged Chinese spy
item.description: US President Donald Trump says the FBI is looking into a matter involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and alleged links to a Chinese government agent. Trump said he had spoken to Huang, who denied knowing the person was a spy, and expressed confidence in the tech executive.

item.title: Pennies Lane: Paul McCartney becomes third richest musician in the world
item.description: Paul McCartney becomes a billionaire, making him the world’s third-richest musician behind Jay-Z and Taylor Swift.

item.title: Oil prices continue to fall on hopes of US-Iran peace deal talks
item.description: Oil prices extend their losses as investors remain hopeful that diplomatic talks between the US and Iran will lead to an end to the Middle East conflict.

item.title: Peru: Giant statue of Pope Leo XIV unveiled ahead of papal visit
item.description: A giant statue of Pope Leo XIV has been unveiled in Callao, Peru, ahead of his upcoming visit. The monument honours the pontiff's close ties to the country, where he previously served as a missionary and bishop.

item.title: How is travel and tourism success measured? This new index aims to shake things up
item.description: The new power, efficiency and opportunity indices from the World Travel & Tourism Council look at economic strength, environmental efficiency and employment opportunity.

item.title: Merz’s budget gamble: no Ukraine funding, no EU budget
item.description: Good morning. I’m Luca Bertuzzi, holding the pen for today’s newsletter. In this edition: Merz ties the EU budget to unanimous financial support for Ukraine, Europe sends a delegation to Abu Dhabi but stays outside the trilateral talks, and the Black Sea strategy struggles to stay afloat.

item.title: California voters reject one-off billionaire wealth tax US media predicts
item.description: The measure was seen as a key test for the global campaign against inequality, but warnings that the super-rich would leave the state won out.

item.title: New K72 app helps Portuguese prepare 72-hour emergency kits for disasters
item.description: The app was created in Montijo by Carlos Batista, in coordination with this municipality's civil protection, but is intended for all Portuguese people and helps them assemble a "kit" for the first 72 hours after a disaster.

item.title: Europe Today: EU joins Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi as race to replace Lagarde heats up
item.description: Ukraine, Russia and the United States resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi, with a joint EU team and officials from France, Germany and the UK on site. We speak to Eurogroup president Kyriakos Pierrakakis about the race to succeed Christine Lagarde and report on new talks over Cyprus's division.

item.title: Countries could save 9 million lives a year by meeting air quality targets they are missing
item.description: Cleaner air could bring far-reaching benefits, from easing pressure on health systems to boosting productivity and economic growth.

item.title: These are Europe’s best hotels and resorts for 2027, according to the Condé Nast Johansens awards
item.description: A design-led hotel within a 14th-century monastery and a property opposite Granada’s cathedral made the cut this year.

item.title: Fossil fuel emissions are expected to fall in 2026. Why aren’t climate experts celebrating?
item.description: Experts warn that a drop in emissions partly driven by conflict and trade disruptions is not sustainable in the long term.

item.title: Who's who from Ukraine and Russia at the Abu Dhabi peace talks?
item.description: The composition of the Ukrainian and Russian delegations at the Abu Dhabi peace talks offers clues to what could be discussed behind closed doors as US-mediated negotiations resume for the first time in nine months.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 10th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 10th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: MWC26 Doha: Mobile economy in MENA set to reach €421bn, but millions remain offline
item.description: MWC26 returned to Doha as the industry faces a dual challenge: building the networks that will power artificial intelligence and narrowing a digital divide that still leaves millions of people without mobile internet.

item.title: Off-season travel: Best times of year to visit some of the world’s most popular destinations
item.description: From autumnal colours in South Korea to touring the Baltics in spring, here are some of Lonely Planet’s top recommendations for travel in off-season.

item.title: Which European country loses the most money when workers strike?
item.description: Ahead of Spain's first joint general strike since 2012, Euronews compares what a day of walkouts costs Europe's economies.

item.title: Republican lawmaker launches eight articles of impeachment against US Defence chief Hegseth
item.description: Republican Kentucky congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment against US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, including alleged violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution, as well as misconduct involving civilian casualties and operations in Yemen and Venezuela.

item.title: Spanish investigation finds over 20,000 suspected paedophile profiles on TikTok
item.description: The foundation Maldita.es reports more than 1,000 child sexual abuse videos found in 35 days of tracking. The Ministry of Youth and Children demands urgent explanations from TikTok and raises the possibility of suspending the platform.

item.title: China's trade surplus surpasses $1 trillion as AI boom powers exports
item.description: China's trade surplus ballooned to more than $1 trillion in October, official data showed on Tuesday, reaching the milestone even earlier than last year's record-breaking sum.

item.title: EU Announces €50 Million for Black Sea Maritime Security Hub in Romania and Bulgaria
item.description: The European funding announcement comes after Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev accused Romania of being indirectly responsible for attacks on commercial ships in the Black Sea. Radev said Bucharest had blamed Russia without providing evidence.

item.title: M John Harrison becomes oldest ever winner of the Booker prize for his satirical novel 'The End of Everything'
item.description: The judges of the prestigious English literary prize praised the novel for it's "extraordinary expert writing and huge ambition" - Harrison is the oldest ever recipient of the prize that is famed for kickstarting careers and says he feels like a proper writer at last.

item.title: Turkey: Steel plant explosion kills 17 in Izmir province
item.description: A devastating explosion at the Habaş iron and steelworks in Aliağa, in western Turkey has killed 17 people. Witnesses described an earthquake-like blast, while footage shows flames, thick smoke and distressed relatives outside the factory.

item.title: Poland: Tusk and Nawrocki honour six victims of Kraków shooting
item.description: Poland's President and Prime Minister set aside their political differences to honour the six victims of a deadly shooting in Kraków. The two leaders laid candles and knelt together at a vigil in the historic city centre.

item.title: Turkey: Delegates arrive in Antalya as COP31 climate talks begin
item.description: The United Nations COP31 climate summit has opened in Antalya after a year marked by deadly heatwaves and devastating floods. Delegates face fresh challenges as the war in Iran disrupts global energy supplies.

item.title: Polish president and PM join Krakow Silent March for victims of market shooting
item.description: Residents of Krakow, led by Poland's president, prime minister and joined by representatives of local government and religious leaders, took part in the March of Silence organised in memory of the victims of Saturday's attack.

item.title: A huge explosion at a steel factory in Western Turkey has left at least 17 people dead and 13 injured
item.description: The explosion occurred when a crane lifting a boiler collapsed into a large industrial furnace, causing a huge fire.

item.title: China's robots, AI agents and Nvidia probe: Web Summit 2026 Opens in Lisbon
item.description: "The superstars of the future are coming from China, not California,” the Web Summit Founder said amid US-China tech tenions.

item.title: How could the Jensen Huang 'spy' scandal affect Nvidia's future?
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces a board investigation over alleged Chinese intelligence links involving a business executive he had an affair with. The allegations raise concerns over security breaches and the future of the world's leading AI chipmaker.

item.title: Argentina: Pope Leo XIV urges Milei's government to protect the most vulnerable
item.description: The Pontiff visited the Cottolengo Don Orione, which cares for over 400 people and has been hit by Javier Milei's cuts, and said a nation's progress should be judged by how it treats those most in need.

item.title: Storm Charles to hit Portugal and Spain with torrential rain and 120 km/h winds
item.description: Strong winds and heavy rain are expected across the Peninsula.

item.title: US drug watchdog orders new safety warnings for weight-loss drugs over potential risk of vision loss
item.description: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is requiring manufacturers of GLP-1 medicines to update their safety labels to warn of a potential increased risk of a rare but serious eye condition that can cause permanent vision loss.

item.title: Argentina: Pope Leo XIV receives warm welcome in Claypole
item.description: Pope Leo XIV was welcomed by crowds in Claypole, near Buenos Aires, as he visited the Don Orione care home. The pontiff greeted the faithful and unveiled a plaque during his 12-day South American tour.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 9th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 9th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: France says Iran behind cyberattacks on supermarket fridges
item.description: French Foreign Minister Barrot said that an investigation into the fridge hack was still underway and that Iran's ambassador to France would be summoned.

item.title: No deal on Ukraine aid? Then no deal on EU budget, Merz says
item.description: The stakes for the EU budget have risen sharply as the German chancellor ties the deal to approving an additional €45 billion for Kyiv. "Supporting Ukraine is a matter of our indivisible European security," Merz said in a letter to Council President Antonio Costa.

item.title: Norway dropped from junior hockey championship to make room for Russia
item.description: The IIHF has moved Norway, ranked 10th, to Division 1A to free a place for Russia at the tournament in Alberta, after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ordered Russian teams reinstated. The change is not yet confirmed, and Russia has not been guaranteed Canadian visas.

item.title: Health gets just a small fraction of climate finance as COP31 warns of growing crisis
item.description: As the health impacts of climate change become increasingly difficult to ignore, COP31 is putting healthcare systems and their ability to adapt at the centre of discussions on the first day of the UN climate conference.

item.title: Ukrainian Foreign Affairs Ministry hits back at hard-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon over Donbas referendum
item.description: The leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party declared that Ukrainians living in the Donbas should be "consulted' on their future.

item.title: Portugal fuel prices drop 9 cents, biggest fall since March
item.description: The week began with a major fuel price drop in Portugal since March, down 9 to 9.5 cents for petrol and diesel; it could be bigger, but the government cut the ISP tax discount.

item.title: Moment judge sentences Russell Brand for rape and sexual assault
item.description: British comedian Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and 6 months in prison after being convicted of rape and three sexual assaults against four women between 2004 and 2009.

item.title: Paris natural history museum acquires 167-million-year-old carnivorous dinosaur skeleton
item.description: The skeleton of a carnivorous dinosaur, the only known specimen of its species, was withdrawn from auction after a deal with the state, to preserve a fossil of outstanding scientific value.

item.title: Ukraine hits Russia’s second-largest refinery as fuel rationing spreads
item.description: Three main processing units at the KINEF plant which handles about 7% of Russia’s refining capacity and supplies St Petersburg’s Pulkovo airport were damaged. Rosneft separately capped fuel sales in six regions, limiting drivers to 30 litres per transaction in cities.

item.title: British comedian Russell Brand sentenced to 10 years and six months for rape, sexual assault
item.description: The British comedian was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault on Thursday following a four-week trial.

item.title: Climate crisis now a health emergency of ‘pandemic scale’, UN climate chief warns
item.description: The United Nations climate chief warns that countries must protect health systems, as climate change poses a growing threat to public health during the climate change conference, COP31, in Turkey.
